meanings.meaning: Java；n.   爪哇（印度尼西亚一岛）

phrases.usage: 出发；启程，指开始一段旅程

examples.en: Both ships set out from Shanghai on June 18th, 1872.
examples.zh: 两艘船于1872年6月18日从上海出发。

examples.en: On the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took the lead.
examples.zh: 在印度洋上，卡蒂萨克号取得了领先。

phrases.usage: 被击中；遭受，指突然遭遇不好的事情

examples.en: In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm.
examples.zh: 八月，她遭遇了一场猛烈的暴风雨。

examples.en: Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
examples.zh: 因此，卡蒂萨克号失去了领先地位。

phrases.usage: （船等）停靠，指在某个港口停留

examples.en: The captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted.
examples.zh: 船长将船停靠在一个港口，让工人安装新舵。

phrases.usage: 左右摇晃，形容船只不稳地晃动

examples.en: The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side and it became impossible to steer her.
examples.zh: 卡蒂萨克号左右摇晃，变得无法操控。

phrases.usage: 困难地安装，形容做某事很艰难

examples.en: A temporary rudder was made and it was fitted with great difficulty.
examples.zh: 一个临时舵被制造出来，但安装得非常困难。

phrases.usage: 毫无疑问...，用于强调确信某事

examples.en: There is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder she would have won the race easily.
examples.zh: 毫无疑问，如果她没有失去舵，她会轻松赢得比赛。

examples.en: Before they were replaced by steamships, sailing vessels were used to carry tea.
examples.zh: 在被汽船取代之前，帆船被用来运茶。

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect Tense)
grammar.definition: 表示在过去某个时间点之前已经完成的动作或状态，常与一般过去时连用 用于描述发生在过去之前的事件，常用于复合句中

examples.en: The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae.
examples.zh: 比赛开始后，第一艘到达爪哇的船是Thermopylae号。

examples.en: She had had many delays before arriving in England.
examples.zh: 她在到达英国之前经历了许多延误。

grammar.title: 虚拟语气 (Subjunctive Mood) - 与过去事实相反
grammar.structure: if + 主语 + had + 过去分词, 主语 + would/could/might have + 过去分词
grammar.definition: 用来表达与事实相反的假设或不可能发生的情况 用于谈论与过去事实相反的假设

examples.en: If she had not lost her rudder, she would have won the race easily.
examples.zh: 如果她没有失去舵，她本会轻松赢得比赛。

examples.en: If it had not rained, we would have gone out.
examples.zh: 如果没有下雨，我们本会出去。

grammar.title: 过去分词作定语 (Past Participle as Adjective)
grammar.structure: 过去分词 + 名词 或 名词 + 过去分词
grammar.definition: 过去分词可用作形容词，修饰名词，表示被动或完成的意义 用于简化定语从句，使句子更简洁

examples.zh: 唯一能与她匹敌的另一艘船是Thermopylae号。

examples.en: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
examples.zh: 她作为一个令人印象深刻的纪念物，提醒人们过去伟大的船只。

translation:
人们在格林威治仍可看到19世纪最有名的帆船之一“卡蒂萨克”号。它停在陆地上，每年接待成千上万的参观者。它给人们留下深刻的印象，使人们回忆起历史上的巨型帆船，在蒸汽船取代帆船之前。“卡蒂萨克”号之类的帆船被用来从中国运回茶叶，从澳大利亚运回羊毛。“卡蒂萨克”号是帆船制造史上建造的最快的一艘帆船。唯一可以与之一比高低的是“塞姆皮雷”号帆船。两船于1872年6月18日同时从上海启航驶往英国，途中展开了一场激烈的比赛。这场比赛持续了整整4个月，是这类比赛中的最后一次，它标志着帆船伟大传统的结束与一个新纪元的开始。
比赛开始后，“赛姆皮雷”号率先抵达爪哇岛。但在印度洋上，“卡萨萨克”号驶到了前面。看来，它首先返抵英国是确信无疑的了，但它却在比赛中连遭厄运。8月份“卡蒂萨克”号遭到一场特大风暴的袭击，失去了一只舵。船身左右摇晃，无法操纵。船员用备用的木板在船上赶制了一只应急用的舵，并克服重重困难将舵安装就位，这样一来，大大降低了船的航速。因为船不能开得太快，否则就有危险，应急舵也会被刮走。因为这个缘故，“卡蒂萨克”号落到了后面。跨越赤道后，船长将船停靠在一个港口，在那儿换了一只舵。但此时，“赛姆皮雷”号早已在500多英里之遥了。尽管换装新舵时分秒必争，但“卡蒂萨克”号已经不可能取胜了，它抵达英国时比“塞姆皮雷”号晚了1个星期。但考虑到路上的多次耽搁，这个成绩也已很不容易了。毫无疑问，如果中途没有失去舵， “卡帝萨克”号肯定能在比赛中轻易夺冠。

lines.en: One of the most famous sailing ships of the nineteenth century, the Cutty Sark, can still be seen at Greewich.
She stands on dry land and is visited by thousands of people each year.
She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of past.
Before they were replaced by steamships , sailing vessels like the Cutty Sark were used to carry tea from China and wool from Australia.
The Cutty Sark was one the fastest sailing ships that has ever been built.
The only other ship to match her was the Thermopylae.
Both these ships set out from Shanghai on June 18th, 1872 on an exciting race to England.
This race, which went on for exactly four exactly four months, was the last of its kind.
It marked the end of the great tradition of ships with sails and the beginning of a new era.
The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae, but on the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took lead.
It seemed certain that she would be the first ship home, but during the race she had a lot of bad luck.
In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm during which her rudder was torn away.
The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side and it became impossible to steer her.
A temporary rudder was made on board from spare planks and it was fitted with great difficulty.
This greatly reduced the speed of the ship, for there was a danger that if she traveled too quickly, this rudder would be torn away as well.
Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
After crossing the Equator, the captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted, but by now the Thermopylae was over five hundred miles ahead.
Though the new rudder was fitted at tremendous speed, it was impossible for the Cutty Sark to win.
She arrived in England a week after the Thermopylae.
Even this was remarkable , considering that she had had so many delays.
These is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder she would have won the race easily.
